the multidrug-binding pockets of the major facilitator superfamily transporters are very versatile and can bind a variety of structurally dissimilar compounds in a multitude of binding modes.
the QacR multidrug-binding pocket is able to accommodate a variety of positively charged drugs, including monovalent, bivalent, and even trivalent compounds.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QacR multidrug-binding pocket is a highly dynamic and versatile binding site that accommodates a variety of structurally diverse drugs.

the binding of pentamidine and dequalinium to QacR is very similar, whereas the binding of hexamidine to QacR differs significantly from both pentamidine and the binding of dequalinium to the related multidrug-binding protein Tet repressor.
the QacR multidrug-binding pocket is able to accommodate a wide variety of structurally diverse cationic drugs and can accommodate both formal positive and neutralized positive charges.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the multidrug-binding pockets of multidrug-binding proteins have the capacity to bind drugs of varying length and charge and that the mechanism by which positively charged drugs bind is likely to be highly variable.
the QacR multidrug-binding pocket is a very accommodating space that can bind a variety of structurally dissimilar compounds in multiple ways.

the binding of positively charged drugs to the multidrug-binding proteins QacR, QacS, and QacB is not restricted to a single mode, and the binding of a drug to a protein does not necessarily imply its efflux.
